guard_streams.source: Statement: Promoting competition and investment in fibre networks - Telecoms Access Review 2026-31
guard_streams.write_limit: Fixed-market regulation, postcode-sector classifications and investment policy are not exact parcel coverage or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Telecoms Access Review statement on 17 March 2026.
The consultation process is recorded as Statement Published and closed.
The statement page was last updated on 13 May 2026.
The decisions apply to fixed telecoms market regulation from April 2026 to March 2031.
The regulated fixed markets underpin broadband, mobile and business connections.
The decisions are designed to promote competition and investment in gigabit-capable networks.
The statement publishes seven main volumes covering overview, markets, remedies, pricing, service quality, reporting and legal instruments.
Supporting files include WLA, LLA and DFA postcode-sector classifications.
Supporting cost models include fibre, dark-fibre, PIA and Area 3 RAB material.
Market and postcode-sector classifications are not treated as exact availability for a selected parcel.

guard_streams.source: New rules to thwart text message scammers and protect consumers and businesses
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile anti-fraud rules, message blocking and caller-ID guidance do not establish fixed-broadband coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the finalised scam-message rules and guidance on 15 July 2026.
The source reports fraud as an estimated 45% of reported crime incidents in England and Wales.
The source reports £1.28 billion lost to criminals in 2025.
Four in ten UK mobile users reported at least one suspicious message in the preceding three months.
The source estimates mobile providers already block more than 600 million scam messages per year.
Providers must block numbers used by scammers and prevent messages being sent from them.
Providers must identify and block scam messages in transit using malicious links and phone numbers.
Mobile providers must set messaging-volume limits for pay-as-you-go SIM cards.
Business-message senders require upfront and ongoing Know Your Customer and Know Your Traffic checks.
Users can report scam calls and messages to 7726 for provider monitoring and protection updates.
